lead_headline: Council Advances Ethics Hearing Against Councilmember Davis, Passes Housing Bonds

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council held its August 18, 2026 business meeting, recognizing faith organizations for their homelessness response, receiving a midyear financial report and drought update, and hearing from the Transportation Advisory Committee. The council passed several resolutions including two affordable housing bond allocations, an emergency preparedness agreement, and a Vision Zero traffic safety commitment, and advanced a second ethics complaint against Councilmember Sharon Davis to a public hearing.

tonight_at_a_glance.synopsis: Council approved regional affordable housing bond allocations, an emergency shelter agreement with Westminster Public Schools, and a Vision Zero resolution, while voting 5–1 to set a public ethics hearing for Councilmember Sharon Davis.
highlights: First ethics complaint against Councilmember Davis dismissed on a code technicality; second complaint advanced to a formal hearing (5–1)
Approximately $10.9 million in private activity bonds assigned to an Adams County affordable housing project (7–0)
Additional $5.3 million in bonds to be carried forward for a Denver senior rehab project in partnership with Jefferson County (7–0)
Vision Zero resolution adopting the Federal Highway Administration Safe System Approach passed unanimously on consent
City's general fund reserve sits at roughly 40%, well above the required 17% minimum, per midyear financial report

prose_paragraphs: The city's general fund reserve stands at approximately $65.5 million, roughly 40% — well above the required 17% minimum. Revenues are running 6.6% above budget (against a 3.3% projection), driven largely by sales tax and property tax, while expenditures have grown 4.3% against a 2% target, partly due to planned transfers to streets and capital improvement funds. The Finance Department flagged warning lights on the city's risk management fund due to insurance cost increases and several pending claims, and on parks due to high fuel costs. Staff cautioned that consumer savings rates have fallen to a 20-year low of 3%, suggesting revenue growth may flatten. The city's investment portfolio is benchmarked at 3.71% return, and the city has applied for approximately $230 million in grants, including two large federal transportation grants expected to be decided in September.

prose_paragraphs: Arvada is experiencing an extreme drought — escalated from 'severe' since the June 16 council presentation — with the US Drought Monitor placing the area in the red 'extreme' category. The city has investigated over 475 waste-of-water complaints and issued more than 250 violation notices, the majority of which are first-offense warnings. July water use came in 14% below the five-year average, and August is tracking toward the 20% savings goal set by council. Denver Water has announced it plans to formalize an end to the irrigation season on October 1, and because 75% of Arvada's water supply comes through Denver Water contracts, Arvada will be required to align its rules accordingly — effectively prohibiting grass watering after September 30. Staff plan to update administrative rules following Denver Water's board meeting the following week and will return to council ahead of spring to discuss extending the drought declaration and potentially implementing surcharges if the drought continues.

prose_paragraphs: TAC Chair Jesse Dubin presented the committee's priorities for 2026: (1) a recommendation on mobility-on-demand transit to address last-mile gaps, particularly in the Candelas neighborhood which has no transit service; (2) a study of roundabouts as a traffic safety tool; and (3) an exploration of land use and transportation, including paid parking in Old Town. The committee reviewed two existing on-demand transit models — Denver's Montbello Connector (operated by VIA Transportation, 100% free to riders) and Lone Tree's Link on Demand (started as a public-private partnership, now expanded to neighboring municipalities) — and found RTD's grant program could cover up to 80% of costs for such a program. Regarding the proposed Route 72 bus extension to Candelas, RTD identified three barriers: uncertain ridership, no safe pedestrian infrastructure along Indiana, and no driver relief station. The committee also unanimously recommended adoption of the Vision Zero plan, which was included in the consent agenda. The committee sent letters of support for grants related to the 72nd Avenue rail crossing.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-054, a resolution authorizing the expenditure of city of Arvvada human resources funding pool funds for 2026 to agencies providing emergency help program assistance and other assistance to Arvvada citizens.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Authorizes spending from the city's HR funding pool to agencies that provide emergency financial assistance to Arvada residents.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-055, a resolution authorizing the issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $860,250 to SIL Terar Motors, Inc. for the purchase of 18 Ford trucks.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Approves a purchase order totaling $860,250 to buy 18 Ford trucks for city fleet use.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-056, a resolution accepting an annexation petition concerning water treatment plant parcel number one, finding said petition substantially compliant with CRS 31-12-1071 and setting a public hearing for October 6, 2026 at 6:15 p.m. for city council to determine whether the area meets the requirements of CRS 31-12-104 and 105 and is considered eligible for annexation.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Accepts a petition to annex a parcel associated with a water treatment plant and schedules a formal annexation eligibility hearing for October 6, 2026.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-057, a resolution accepting an annexation petition concerning water treatment plant parcel number two, finding said petition substantially compliant with CRS 31-12-1071 and setting a public hearing for October 6, 2026 at 6:15 p.m. for city council to determine whether the area meets the requirements of CRS 31-12-104 and 105 and is considered eligible for annexation.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Accepts a second petition to annex a parcel associated with a water treatment plant and schedules the same October 6, 2026 hearing for eligibility determination.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-058, a resolution adopting the Federal Highway Administration safe system approach to inform city plans and actions as the city works toward a quote vision zero goal of eliminating fatalities and serious injuries resulting from traffic accidents.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Formally commits Arvada to the Vision Zero framework, adopting the federal Safe System Approach as the guiding principle for reducing traffic deaths and serious injuries to zero. The Transportation Advisory Committee unanimously recommended this resolution.

resolutions.official_title: R26-059, a resolution authorizing the assignment of City of Arvvada's private activity bond allocation to the Housing Authority of the County of Adams, State of Colorado, doing business as Maker Housing Partners, pursuant to the Colorado Private Activity Bond Sealing Allocation Act.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Assigns approximately $10.9 million in Arvada private activity bonds (combining 2025 carry-forward and 2026 allocation) to Maker Housing Partners to support a 130-unit, 100% affordable housing development at 68th and Lowell Boulevard in unincorporated Adams County. The project uses 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. Arvada will receive credit toward its Proposition 123 affordable housing unit commitments.

resolutions.official_title: R26-060, a resolution declaring the intent of the city of Arvvada to issue revenue bonds in connection with the financing residential facilities for low and middle income families or persons.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Carries forward approximately $5.3 million in remaining 2026 private activity bonds, to be assigned to a joint Jefferson County–Denver project supporting a 188-unit senior affordable housing rehabilitation project in northwestern Denver. A unit-sharing agreement among Arvada, Jefferson County, and Denver for Proposition 123 credit is anticipated.

resolutions.official_title: R26-061, a resolution authorizing an intergovernmental agreement by and between Westminster Public Schools and the city of Arvvada for the activation and operation of a public information center in the event of an emergency.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Creates a formal agreement with Westminster Public Schools to use a school facility on Arvada's eastern side as a public information center during disasters. Arvada would staff the information function; Westminster Public Schools would operate the facility and be reimbursed for 50% of documented costs, with the city seeking FEMA reimbursement.

resolutions.official_title: R26-062, a resolution pursuant to section 2-378 of the Arvvada City Code determining that it is more likely than not that a violation of section 2-37510 did not occur because of a technical deficiency in the city's adopted code of ethics and therefore determining to dismiss the complaint alleging misconduct of council member Sharon Davis.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Dismisses the first ethics complaint against Councilmember Sharon Davis on the grounds that a technical deficiency in the city's code of ethics means a violation more likely than not did not occur under the applicable provision.

resolutions.official_title: R26-063, a resolution pursuant to section 2-378 of the Arvvada City Code, determining that it is more likely than not that a violation of section 2-3751 of the Arvvada Code did occur and setting a hearing pursuant to section 2-378E2 of the Arvvada code to be conducted pursuant to section 2-379 of the code.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Finds it more likely than not that a second ethics violation by Councilmember Sharon Davis did occur — related to an allegation of disclosing executive session information — and sets the matter for a formal quasi-judicial public hearing. Councilmember Davis's attorney, Christopher Beal, argued procedurally that council members are witnesses to the central defense and should not sit in judgment, and that the resolution does not identify a special prosecutor. Councilmember Griffith cast the sole dissenting vote, citing cost concerns and the lack of precedent.

public_hearings.what_is_being_heard: CB26-018, an ordinance amending section 102-182 (water surcharges) of chapter 102 (utilities) of the Arvada city code, ordinance number 4934. This item had been previously scheduled for a public hearing this evening in connection with drought-related water surcharges. The item was removed from the agenda before the meeting.

vote_breakdown.motion_text: Item removed from agenda — no vote taken.

public_hearings.follow_up_direction: Staff indicated they will return with a drought declaration extension and potential surcharge proposal ahead of spring 2027 if drought conditions persist.
